entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-97jf-46m3-8953: Security feature bypass vulnerability in Azure Key Vault Keys library for Java
entry.content:
Security feature bypass vulnerability in Azure Key Vault Keys library for Java

Aliases: CVE-2026-33117

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • com.azure:azure-security-keyvault-keys — fixed in 4.10.6

The Java Key Vault Keys library in the Azure SDK for Java contains an issue in the local cryptographic verification path where authentication tag comparison was implemented incorrectly. In affected applications that use the vulnerable local cryptography path, specially crafted encrypted input may bypass integrity verification checks. Operations delegated to the Key Vault service are not affected. The issue is addressed in version 4.10.6.

Bootstrap Vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting

Aliases: CVE-2019-8331

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

For `bootstrap` 3.x upgrade to 3.4.1 or later.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-3g76-f9xq-8vp6: Vert.x has a DoS via unbounded server-side SNI SslContext cache growth
entry.content:
Vert.x has a DoS via unbounded server-side SNI SslContext cache growth

Aliases: CVE-2026-6860

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:L

Affected:

  • io.vertx:vertx-core
  • io.vertx:vertx-core
  • io.vertx:vertx-core — fixed in 4.5.27
  • io.vertx:vertx-core — fixed in 5.0.12

Potential unbounded server-side SNI `SslContext` cache growth in Vert.x TLS handling, with = resource-exhaustion / DoS impact. On affected versions, matching server-side SNI names are cached via `computeIfAbsent(serverName, ...)` in a serverName-keyed `SslContext` cache. The implementation differs slightly by branch, but the same sink appears to be present in released versions `4.3.4` through `5.0.11`: - `4.3.x`: `SSLHelper` - `4.4.x` / `4.5.x`: `SslChannelProvider` - `5.0.x` and current `master`: `SslContextProvider` When server-side SNI is enabled and wildcard or otherwise broad hostname mappings are used, an unauthenticated client can send many distinct matching SNI names and cause the server to retain increasing numbers of `SslContext` entries over time, leading to increasing memory …

entry.content:
CC-Tweaked has an SSRF Protection Bypass with NAT64

Aliases: CVE-2026-47695

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H

Affected:

  • cc.tweaked:cc-tweaked-1.21-core — fixed in 1.119.0
  • cc.tweaked:cc-tweaked-1.20.1-core — fixed in 1.119.0
  • cc.tweaked:cc-tweaked-1.20.4-core — fixed in 1.119.0
  • cc.tweaked:cc-tweaked-1.20.5-core — fixed in 1.119.0
  • cc.tweaked:cc-tweaked-1.20.6-core — fixed in 1.119.0
  • cc.tweaked:cc-tweaked-1.19.3-core — fixed in 1.119.0
  • cc.tweaked:cc-tweaked-1.19.4-core — fixed in 1.119.0
  • cc.tweaked:cc-tweaked-1.20-core — fixed in 1.119.0

### Summary CC-Tweaked's HTTP API (`http.request`, `http.websocket`) blocks requests to private network ranges to prevent server-side request forgery (SSRF). This protection can be bypassed on IPv6-capable servers using NAT64 well-known prefix addresses (`64:ff9b::/96`). An attacker who can execute Lua code can reach any internal IPv4 service that the filter is intended to block, by addressing it as `http://[64:ff9b::<ipv4-as-hex>]/` instead of its direct IPv4 address. This affects any CC-Tweaked deployment on a network with NAT64 routing — a configuration that is standard on AWS, GCP, and other cloud platforms when using IPv6-only subnets. ### Details The IP filter in [`PrivatePattern.matches()` (AddressPredicate.java#L121–L130)](https://github.com/cc-tweaked/CC-Tweaked/blob/663ffed433…

entry.content:
Yamcs vulnerable to unauthorized user enumeration via IAM API endpoints

Aliases: CVE-2026-44595

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

### Summary The IAM API endpoints (`listUsers`, `getUser`, `listGroups`, and `getGroup`) in `yamcs-core` do not enforce the required `SystemPrivilege.ControlAccess` check.
